record.original_question: Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_{k>=0} a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that the diagonal operator T[x^k]=((1+k+k^2)/k!)x^k never increases the number of nonreal zeros of a real polynomial?

evidence.quote: Problem 37. Is the sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!}_0^infinity a CZDS?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real polynomial $p(x) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$, let $Z_c(p)$ denote the number of nonreal zeros of $p$, counted with multiplicity. A sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if the diagonal linear operator $T$ defined on polynomials by $T[x^k] = \gamma_k x^k$ satisfies
$$Z_c(T[p(x)]) \le Z_c(p(x))$$
for every real polynomial $p(x)$.

Determine whether the sequence
$$\gamma_k = \frac{1 + k + k^2}{k!}, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
is a complex zero decreasing sequence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on complex zero decreasing sequences. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving whether the specific sequence {(1+k+k^2)/k!} is CZDS; related work continues to study sufficient conditions for the CZDS property without settling this concrete instance.

status_evidence.title: Complex Zero Decreasing Sequences (Craven–Csordas)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational survey discussing CZDS, characterizations, and open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background but does not resolve the specific test sequence.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:1505.00355
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of whether {(1+k+k^2)/k!} is a CZDS as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Posed as an open problem with no later resolution found.
